references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew: A servant girl recognizes Peter and confronts him by the fire. "A servant girl came to him and said, 'You also were with Jesus of Galilee'" ([ref:Matt 26:69|Matthew 26:69]).
The parallel passage in Mark: One of the high priest's servant girls sees Peter warming himself and says that he was with Jesus of Nazareth ([ref:Mark 14:66-67|Mark 14:66-67]).
The parallel passage in John: The servant girl who guarded the gate asks Peter, "Are you not also one of this man's disciples?" ([ref:Joh 18:17|John 18:17]).

The immediate context: Peter followed Jesus at a distance and sat among those who had lit a fire in the courtyard – this is the situation in which the servant girl observes him ([ref:Luk 22:54-55|Luke 22:54-55]).
Peter's first denial follows immediately after the servant girl's accusation: "Woman, I do not know him" ([ref:Luk 22:57|Luke 22:57]).

Jesus' prediction about Peter's denial: "Peter, before the rooster crows today, you will deny three times that you know me" – the servant girl's recognition is the beginning of the fulfillment of this prophecy ([ref:Luk 22:34|Luke 22:34]).

The Acts of the Apostles describes how opponents recognized Peter and John as people who "had been with Jesus" – the same expression used by the servant girl in Luke 22:56 (σὺν αὐτῷ ἦν) ([ref:Apg 4:13|Acts 4:13]).
